prerequisites: Ordinary Linear Differential Equations with constant coefficients
Fourier Transform and spectral description of signals
Calculation and representation of system responses (impulse response, step response, frequency response)

learning_outcomes.text: Students know the fundamentals of metrology and sensor technology.
Students know the scientifically correct evaluation, documentation, and interpretation of measurement results.
They know commonly used sensors, transducers, and flow sensors.
Furthermore, they know the basic principles of digital measurement technology and the objective of digital measurement signal processing.
They know important digital counting circuits and analog-to-digital converters.
Thus, students know the sampling theorem and can interpret a measurement signal as a time signal and as a spectrum.
Students can statistically evaluate measurement series and make a statement about the uncertainty of the measured value.
Students can also implement basic electrical measurement circuits (design of measurement bridges, dimensioning of amplifier, filter, and computing circuits).
They can select and adjust measurement lines and probes and select a suitable analog-to-digital converter for a measurement task.
They can also select suitable flow sensors.
They can independently study the contents of the lecture using a textbook.
Students can independently work out the solutions to the exercise problems.
Furthermore, students know how metrological solutions and systems are to be evaluated and selected.
They understand what influences the transfer behavior of a sensor element has on the measurement result and how the transfer behavior can be determined.
They know how to correctly use a measurement system and how to evaluate the measurement data.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of Measurement Technology and Sensor Technology: General principles of Measurement Technology, SI unit system
Basic properties of sensors and measurement processes; Characteristic curves and transfer behavior of sensors and measurement systems
Fundamentals of Measurement Data Evaluation: Statistics, determination of statistical measurement uncertainties, sensitivity analysis for systematic influences
Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering: Calculation with impedances, introduction of electrical measurands
Classic electrical measuring devices: Moving coil and moving iron measuring instruments, oscilloscope
Sensors: Introduction of various sensor elements for a range of important physical measurands that respond with resistance, voltage, current, capacitance or inductance changes
Analog electrical measurement technology: Design of measurement bridges for real and complex impedances, dimensioning of amplifier, filter, and computing circuits, selection of measurement lines

Digital Measurement Technology: Basic structures of digital systems, sampling theorem, digital filters, counting circuits, digital-analog / analog-digital converters, encoders, digital signals in time and frequency domain
